claims.title: Flooding matchmaking can exhaust the lobby and its player-database dependency
claims.description: An attacker operating `process:game-client` on a player-controlled machine can send large volumes of matchmaking requests over `flow:game-client-to-lobby:matchmaking`, which crosses from `boundary:player-local-machine` into production. `process:lobby` must read `store:player-database` to form a match and then hand work to `process:game-servers`; therefore each cheap TCP request can consume lobby connection, CPU, and match-formation capacity as well as database-read capacity. Authentication on the client-to-lobby flow is `unknown`, so this is conditional on requests being accepted without an effective identity-bound rate or concurrency limit. Second-order, saturating `process:lobby`, which is tagged `availability-critical`, prevents legitimate matchmaking; pressure propagated to `store:player-database` can also delay its reads and writes by `process:game-servers` and `process:moderation-website`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high, conditional on the unknown authentication state of `flow:game-client-to-lobby:matchmaking`: the derived crossing admits traffic from player-controlled machines, and `process:lobby` is stated to be internet-facing. Impact is high because `process:lobby` is tagged `availability-critical`, and its failure blocks matchmaking while its database dependency is shared with `process:game-servers` and `process:moderation-website`.

mitigations.summary: Apply identity-bound admission controls to matchmaking
mitigations.detail: Authenticate clients before costly match formation and enforce per-account, per-source, and per-device rate and concurrent-request limits on `flow:game-client-to-lobby:matchmaking`.

mitigations.summary: Bound matchmaking work and isolate database capacity
mitigations.detail: Set request and queue limits, short timeouts, and load shedding in `process:lobby`; reserve bounded `store:player-database` connection and query capacity so matchmaking bursts cannot starve game-server or moderation work.

claims.title: Held or flooded gameplay connections can exhaust game-server match capacity
claims.description: A player-controlled attacker can open or retain many TCP 1235 connections on `flow:game-client-to-game-servers:gameplay-traffic`, or send high-rate gameplay actions and state updates, to consume `process:game-servers` connection slots, per-match memory, and processing capacity at far lower cost than maintaining the resulting server-side sessions. The flow crosses from `boundary:player-local-machine` and its authentication is `unknown`, so the threat is conditional on the absence or insufficiency of authenticated per-client connection, message-rate, and idle-time bounds. Second-order, exhaustion of `process:game-servers`, tagged `availability-critical`, disconnects or prevents play for legitimate players and prevents the service from recording outcomes to `store:stats-database` and player progression to `store:player-database`.

mitigations.summary: Shed load before match capacity is depleted
mitigations.detail: Use bounded per-match queues and server-side resource budgets in `process:game-servers`; reject excess work quickly rather than allowing it to consume memory, worker capacity, or database-write capacity.

claims.title: A player-controlled client may obtain another player's matchmaking authority
claims.description: A player starts on the uncontrolled `process:game-client` in `boundary:player-local-machine` and reaches `process:lobby` over `flow:game-client-to-lobby:matchmaking`, which crosses out of the tenant boundary and has `authentication: unknown`. If `process:lobby` does not bind each matchmaking request and player identifier to a verified player and authorize it server-side, a player can submit another player's identifiers and cause the lobby to act with matchmaking authority beyond their own account. Second-order, `process:lobby` reads player account records through `flow:lobby-to-player-database:read-players`, so the authorization boundary protects access to player-record information as well as match placement.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `authentication` on `flow:game-client-to-lobby:matchmaking`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high, conditional on the unstated authentication and server-side authorization on `flow:game-client-to-lobby:matchmaking`: a player already controls `process:game-client` on the derived crossing into production. Impact is medium because the gained authority reaches player account records in `store:player-database`, which is tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Bind matchmaking actions to the verified player identity
mitigations.detail: Have `process:lobby` authenticate the caller on `flow:game-client-to-lobby:matchmaking`, derive the player identity from that credential rather than request identifiers, and authorize every requested matchmaking action against that identity.

mitigations.summary: Reject untrusted player identifiers
mitigations.detail: Treat player identifiers supplied by `process:game-client` as references only; enforce ownership and match-membership checks in `process:lobby` before reading or acting on the associated player record.

claims.title: A modified game client may gain authority to submit outcomes for other players or matches
claims.description: A player controls `process:game-client` on hardware outside the operator's control and directly reaches `process:game-servers` over `flow:game-client-to-game-servers:gameplay-traffic`, a crossing from `boundary:player-local-machine` into `boundary:prod-network` whose `authentication` is unknown. If the game servers do not authenticate the client and enforce that every gameplay action belongs to the caller's assigned player and active match, the player can send well-formed actions or state updates for another player or match and obtain authority beyond their own game session. Second-order, `process:game-servers` records match statistics through `flow:game-servers-to-stats-database:read-write-stats` and writes player progression and match results through `flow:game-servers-to-player-database:update-players`, allowing the gained authority to alter business-critical match and player records.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `authentication` on `flow:game-client-to-game-servers:gameplay-traffic`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high, conditional on the unknown authentication and authorization state of `flow:game-client-to-game-servers:gameplay-traffic`, because any player controls the crossing source `process:game-client`. Impact is medium because the resulting authority can write `store:stats-database` and `store:player-database`, both tagged `business-critical-data`, while the player database also contains `pii`.

mitigations.summary: Enforce server-side player and match authorization
mitigations.detail: Authenticate each client connection at `process:game-servers`, derive the player identity and assigned match from the verified session, and reject gameplay messages that target another player, match, or state transition.

mitigations.summary: Constrain database writes to validated game state
mitigations.detail: Ensure `process:game-servers` writes over `flow:game-servers-to-stats-database:read-write-stats` and `flow:game-servers-to-player-database:update-players` only after server-authoritative validation, with database grants limited to the required update operations.

claims.title: Players may deny match actions because outcomes cannot be tied to a verified player identity
claims.description: A player operating the uncontrolled `process:game-client` can send gameplay actions over `flow:game-client-to-game-servers:gameplay-traffic` to the internet-facing `process:game-servers`. The flow's `authentication` is unknown; if it does not establish and propagate an individual player identity, a player can dispute gameplay actions or a resulting match outcome and `process:game-servers` cannot produce evidence binding that action to them. The model also contains no `audit` element or audit flow for these sensitive writes. This affects outcomes written by `process:game-servers` to `store:stats-database` and `store:player-database`, so disputes can undermine the evidential value of match statistics and player progression across all matches, not merely one connection. This is conditional on the unstated authentication and audit-recording design, not an assertion that either control is absent.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high, conditional on the unknown authentication design: `flow:game-client-to-game-servers:gameplay-traffic` crosses from the player-controlled zone and reaches the internet-facing `process:game-servers`, so any player can initiate disputed gameplay. Impact is medium because the affected outcomes reach `store:stats-database` and player records, which carry `business-critical-data`, but the model does not establish financial or credential compromise.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate and retain the individual player identity for gameplay actions
mitigations.detail: Use an individual, verified player session or token on `flow:game-client-to-game-servers:gameplay-traffic`, and have `process:game-servers` record its validated subject rather than a self-reported player identifier.

mitigations.summary: Create an independent match-action audit trail
mitigations.detail: Have `process:game-servers` emit structured, tamper-resistant audit events for match actions and outcomes, including actor, match ID, target, timestamp, sequence/order, and outcome, to a dedicated audit store separate from the game-write path.

claims.title: Unverified gameplay connections could let attackers act as other players
claims.description: `flow:game-client-to-game-servers:gameplay-traffic` crosses from the player-controlled `boundary:player-local-machine` to internet-facing `process:game-servers`, while its `authentication` attribute is unknown. If the game server does not verify a player-bound session or equivalent identity on that flow, an attacker can connect from their own `process:game-client` and send gameplay traffic as another `entity:player`. Second-order, `process:game-servers` records match statistics in `store:stats-database` and writes match outcomes and progression to `store:player-database`, so the impersonation can affect business-critical match records and player records. This draft is conditional on the unverified authentication attribute.

Second-order, altered actions can change match outcomes and are recorded through `flow:game-servers-to-stats-database:read-write-stats` and `flow:game-servers-to-player-database:update-players` as match statistics, progression, and results.

mitigations.detail: Configure `flow:game-client-to-game-servers:gameplay-traffic` with TLS or another protocol providing authenticated encryption, and record the verified authentication method.

claims.title: Support moderation traffic may expose player-account information in transit

If the link is not effectively encrypted, a malicious insider or an attacker with an on-path position in the corporate or production network can intercept account-associated PII and moderation activity while it travels to `process:moderation-website`. The disclosed account context can enable targeted social engineering of players or support staff and helps an attacker focus later attempts against the player-account read path to `store:player-database`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on the unknown channel controls because the attacker must first gain an on-path position between the corporate and production networks. mitigations.summary: Use authenticated TLS for moderation access

claims.title: Unverified write authentication may permit direct alteration of player records

If either unresolved write path does not authenticate and authorize its caller with least-privilege write scope, an attacker who reaches that path can alter player progression, match results, account records, or moderation state directly in `store:player-database`, bypassing the intended application workflow. Second-order, `process:lobby` reads player records through `flow:lobby-to-player-database:read-players`, and the game servers and moderation website also use the altered records as authoritative state.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on the unknown authentication attributes because an attacker must reach a production database write path; the model does not establish that the store is externally reachable.
